requirements.summary: Undo button works with any change
requirements.description_excerpt: Currently undo button reverses last dates change. The plan is to make it work with any editable data type. User should be able to reverse status change, assignee change etc with this button. This includes bulk actions.

acceptance_criteria.text: Currently undo feature is stored on frontend - new mechanism will be backend event sourcing. Dates & scheduling undo mechanism works fine - just needs to be moved to backend
User can revert last X changes.
User can revert changes on any* datatypes (*some exceptions may appear).
User can only undo changes they did.
Page refresh does not remove possibility to undo last change.
Scheduling changes can be undone (like now)
if data was changed in the meantime ... there is an error informing that other changes occurred in the meantime and this undo cannot be applied.
if operation expired (more than 8 hours passed), there is an error when I try to undo it.

in_scope: Must have: undo works with most (or all) fields — status, assignee, description etc., not only dates
Should have: revert more than one change (count undecided)
Should to have: undo of structure changes with cascading date reverts
Phase 1: re-create the current single dates undo on the backend (event sourcing)

findings.excerpt_quote: How to handle undo of more than one operation? Option A: only let undo one operation at a time, the most recent one ... Option C sounds very complex and I don’t think we will implement it this way, but wanted to describe it so we make a conscious decision.
findings.finding_summary: The interaction model for undoing more than one operation is left open between Options A, B and C in the epic's own Questions section, while the Definition of done already assumes multi-change undo.
findings.testing_impact: Cannot define the multi-undo flow, its selection rules or its UI to test until one option is chosen.
findings.question_for_PM: Which of Option A, B or C ships?

findings.excerpt_quote: User can revert last X changes.
findings.finding_summary: Definition of done item "User can revert last X changes" leaves X undefined; the Questions section says only "we can investigate technical feasibility 5 or 10".
findings.testing_impact: No pass/fail assertion on the undo-count limit is possible until X is set.

findings.excerpt_quote: If I cannot undo the most recent change, chan I undo older changes? From business perspective I can suggest to make it possible to revert older changes, but it’s a mild suggestion and technical optimization should be the main driver of the answer here.
findings.finding_summary: Whether older changes stay revertible when the most recent one cannot be undone is raised as open, with only a "mild suggestion" and no decision.
findings.testing_impact: Negative-path tests for the undo history after a failed undo cannot be scoped.
findings.question_for_PM: If the latest change can't be undone, can older ones still be?

findings.excerpt_quote: User can revert changes on any* datatypes (*some exceptions may appear).
findings.finding_summary: No out-of-scope note exists although the change touches shared systems (field editing, bulk actions, scheduling, structure), and the "some exceptions" datatypes are never listed.
findings.testing_impact: Cannot build the field/datatype coverage matrix or know which fields should refuse undo.
findings.question_for_PM: Which fields and datatypes are excluded?

findings.excerpt_quote: Undo/redo support for more fields (currently it’s only task dates)
findings.finding_summary: The linked PRD names this epic "Undo/redo support for more fields", but the epic's scope and Definition of done mention undo only; redo is neither in nor out of scope.
findings.testing_impact: Whether a whole redo test surface exists is unknown, so the epic's test scope cannot be bounded.
findings.question_for_PM: Is redo in scope for this epic?

findings.excerpt_quote: This epic can be broken down into phases: 1. Re-create current single undo of dates on backend 2. Add support to all (or most) data types & editable fields 3. Add support to more than one action undo 4. Add undo of structure changes
findings.finding_summary: The epic describes four delivery phases but has no child work items, so no child description owns any phase; the Q4 planning page nonetheless marks it "Ready for Q4? Yes" with a start date of 2026-10-26.
findings.testing_impact: No child can be scanned or test-planned yet; epic-level coverage cannot be mapped to any story.
findings.question_for_PM: Which child items will carry phases 1–4?

findings.finding_summary: No design reference exists (UX Design status "To decide", PRD Design Artifacts empty, no Figma link) although the Definition of done implies UI validation: an error message is displayed, and Options B and C describe a selectable list of actions.
findings.testing_impact: UI assertions for error messages and any multi-undo list cannot be written without a design reference.
findings.question_for_PM: Will a design reference be produced, and before which phase?

findings.finding_summary: Bulk actions are in scope, but undoing a bulk action where only some items were changed by someone else in the meantime is not described (whole undo refused, partial undo, or per-item errors).
findings.testing_impact: Bulk-undo conflict tests cannot state an expected result; the single-item error path stays testable.

findings.excerpt_quote: Page refresh does not remove possibility to undo last change.
findings.finding_summary: The lifecycle of an undoable action is only partly stated (survives refresh, expires after 8 hours, refused after a conflicting change); what happens to the history after an undo, or when a new change supersedes an undoable one, is not described.
findings.testing_impact: State-transition coverage of the undo history is limited to the three stated rules.

findings.excerpt_quote: Currently it’s 1, we can investigate technical feasibility 5 or 10, and impact of such increase on performance.
findings.finding_summary: The performance impact of raising the undo limit is named by the epic's author as an open investigation, with no target stated.
findings.testing_impact: No performance acceptance threshold exists for undo with a longer history.

findings.finding_summary: Neither the epic nor the linked pages name how the change is released: no feature flag, staged rollout, or statement that it ships to everyone at once, although phase 1 replaces the existing dates undo.
findings.testing_impact: Cannot plan flag-on/flag-off regression of the existing dates undo during rollout.

findings.excerpt_quote: new mechanism will be backend event sourcing
findings.finding_summary: Event sourcing is named as the mechanism, but no logging, audit or metrics for undo actions themselves are mentioned.
findings.testing_impact: Support/debug signals for undo cannot be verified.

findings.finding_summary: No test environment, fixture or data note for exercising undo across many datatypes, concurrent editors, or the 8-hour expiry.
findings.testing_impact: Test setup for concurrency and expiry must be designed from scratch.

findings.excerpt_quote: Ready for Q4? (is on Gantt + has estimates) — Yes
findings.finding_summary: Tracking fields tell different stories: the Q4 planning page marks the epic ready, while it has no children, no fix version, and UX Design status "To decide".
findings.testing_impact: Low impact now; worth aligning before sprint planning picks it up.

questions.question: Which multi-undo model ships — Option A (most recent only), Option B (a list, reverting from the most recent down with no skips) or Option C (chainable/non-chainable)? And, for that option, what is X in "User can revert last X changes", and is the 8-hour time limit confirmed?
questions.context: The Definition of done assumes multi-change undo and an 8-hour expiry, while the Questions section leaves both the option and the limit open ("5 or 10", "I suggest" 8 hours). Option A would make X a fixed one. Resolving X also frames the performance question in RR-ONE-354099-10.
questions.source: Description — Definition of done; Questions section

questions.question: The PRD lists this epic as "Undo/redo support for more fields", but the epic mentions only undo. Is redo in scope? And which fields or datatypes are the "some exceptions" that stay out of scope?
questions.context: The PRD and the epic disagree on redo, and the epic has no out-of-scope list for a change that touches field editing, bulk actions, scheduling and structure.
questions.source: Confluence PRD (appfireteam.atlassian.net, page 99074146305) — Features and Functionality; Description — Definition of done

questions.question: Will a design reference be produced for the undo error messages and any multi-undo list, and before which phase?

questions.question: How will the new backend undo be released — behind a feature flag (name, default, who flips it), staged, or to everyone at once?
questions.context: Phase 1 replaces the existing frontend dates undo, so the release path decides the regression plan.

questions.context: The epic calls the first part "a mild suggestion" left to technical optimization; the bulk case is not mentioned.

qa_readiness_checklist.check: Confirm the multi-undo option, the value of X, and the 8-hour limit
Confirm whether redo is in scope and list excluded fields/datatypes
Confirm a design reference for error messages and any undo list
Confirm the release path (flag, staged, or all at once)
Confirm child items exist for phases 1–4
Confirm undo-history and bulk-undo behaviour after a conflict
Regression-check the existing dates and scheduling undo after the move to backend event sourcing
Check the concurrent-change error using the Assignee A → B → C example
Check the expiry error for an operation older than 8 hours
Check that a user cannot undo another user's change, and that undo survives a page refresh

report.readiness_line: Seven High findings stand between this epic and a testable scope — chiefly the undecided multi-undo model and limit (RR-ONE-354099-01, RR-ONE-354099-02, Q1) and the redo and exclusion boundary (RR-ONE-354099-05, Q2) — and the epic has no child items yet (Q5).

facts.text: Business goal: "Currently undo button reverses last dates change. The plan is to make it work with any editable data type. User should be able to reverse status change, assignee change etc with this button. This includes bulk actions."

Must have: undo works with most (or all) fields; Should have: revert more than one change; "Should to have": undo of structure changes, which reverts the structure change, the task's dates, and any other tasks' dates affected through dependencies or parent-child relations.
Four phases: re-create the current single dates undo on the backend; add all (or most) data types and editable fields; add undo of more than one action; add undo of structure changes.
The new mechanism is backend event sourcing; the current dates and scheduling undo "works fine - just needs to be moved to backend".
"User can only undo changes they did." and "Page refresh does not remove possibility to undo last change."

An undo is refused with an error when the data changed in the meantime (worked example: Assignee A → B by me, then C by a colleague; undo to A is not possible) or when the operation is more than 8 hours old.
facts.source: Description — Definition of done, Support for errors

facts.text: The undo-count limit is open ("Currently it’s 1, we can investigate technical feasibility 5 or 10"); the 8-hour time limit is offered as "I suggest".

The PRD lists this epic as "Undo/redo support for more fields (currently it’s only task dates)" with priority CRITICAL, under an objective to deliver the navigation "by the end of 2026". Its Success Criteria and Design Artifacts sections are empty.

The Q4 planning page marks this epic "Ready for Q4? Yes". Its estimate cell, in Polish and cut short with an ellipsis in the page itself, translates as: 1. estimate of a new backend mechanism that keeps date undo, which is what the current undo does; 2. extension of that mechanism with… (text ends there).
facts.source: Confluence: Embers 2026 Q4 planning, appfireteam.atlassian.net page 99820732524 (v23)

risks.text: Undo writes data back across tasks; with scheduling and structure cascades (and the "revert all the chainable operations that happened after to be safe" rule sketched in Option C), an undo could revert more than the user intended.
risks.source: Description — Scope of the epic; Questions, Option C

risks.text: Phase 1 moves the working dates and scheduling undo from frontend to backend, so the existing behaviour is a regression surface from day one.
Concurrent edits from Jira or other users drive the main error path; conflict detection must be correct for every newly supported field.
Planning signals readiness for Q4 while the epic has no children, no design reference and open core questions; test planning may start late relative to the 2026-10-26 start.
risks.source: Confluence: Embers 2026 Q4 planning; ONE-354099 fields

testing_focus.text: Regression of the existing dates and scheduling undo once it runs on backend event sourcing (phase 1).
Concurrent-change refusal per newly supported field, starting with the Assignee A → B → C example.
Expiry after 8 hours, including a stale browser tab with an apparently active undo button.
Own-changes-only rule and undo surviving a page refresh.
Multi-undo selection and limit behaviour, once the option and X are chosen.

report.batch_rationale: This epic has no child work items yet — both "Epic Link" and parent JQL returned none — so there is nothing to scan individually. Re-run this review once children exist.
report.next_action: Take Q1, Q2 and Q5 to the PO, Q3 to UX and Q6 to EM; Q4 can follow. Once child items exist for the four phases, rescan this epic and then scan each child.
